content.value_statement: Benchling integrations can be hard to build because registry, inventory, ELN, workflow, and authentication patterns differ. This skill gives focused guidance for SDK and REST API automation with credential, pagination, and workflow examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains Benchling API authentication with API keys, OAuth, OIDC, and environment variables.
Shows SDK patterns for DNA, RNA, protein, custom entity, and mixture operations.
Documents inventory operations for containers, boxes, locations, plates, and transfers.
Guides ELN entry creation, entity linking, and workflow task automation.
Summarizes REST endpoints, pagination, filters, error handling, and retry behavior.
Provides patterns for EventBridge integrations and Data Warehouse analytics.
limitations: Does not include executable connector code or a packaged Benchling client.
Requires valid Benchling tenant access and permissions before examples can run.
Does not validate tenant schemas, field names, folder IDs, or workflow statuses.
Can expose sensitive lab data if users export or share results without controls.

use_cases.title: Build Registry Sync Jobs
use_cases.description: Plan sequence and custom entity synchronization between Benchling and approved internal systems.

use_cases.title: Audit Inventory Locations
use_cases.description: Use SDK patterns to list containers, boxes, and transfers for controlled inventory reviews.

use_cases.title: Prepare Analytics Exports
use_cases.description: Map Benchling data warehouse and API outputs into reports for research and compliance teams.

prompt_templates.title: List Available APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me which Benchling SDK areas this skill covers for registry, inventory, ELN, and workflows. Ask for my tenant and permission context before suggesting calls.

prompt_templates.title: Create Sequence Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a Benchling DNA sequence creation workflow using the Python SDK. Include authentication, folder and schema inputs, field mapping, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Inventory Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inventory audit script for containers in a Benchling box. Include pagination, error handling, least-privilege credentials, and safe export handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Event Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an event-driven Benchling integration that routes selected events through AWS EventBridge to downstream systems. Include failure handling, retries, and data minimization.

output_examples.input: I need to create DNA sequence records in Benchling from a controlled import file.
output: A required-input checklist for tenant URL, folder, schema, registry, and credential source.
A validation plan for sequence names, bases, schema fields, and duplicate handling.
A safe rollout plan that starts with a small staging import before production.

output_examples.input: I want to audit all containers inside a freezer box and share a report.
output: A paginated inventory query plan that limits API load and handles missing permissions.
Recommended report fields for identifiers, locations, barcodes, and status values.
Data handling notes for sensitive sample metadata and approved storage locations.

output_examples.input: I need an event integration for workflow task status changes.
output: An EventBridge routing design with filtering before downstream processing.
Failure handling recommendations for retries, dead-letter queues, and audit logs.
A data minimization checklist for payload fields sent outside Benchling.

best_practices: Use environment variables or a secret manager for API credentials.
Start with read-only permissions and expand access only when required.
Filter and paginate server-side before exporting Benchling data.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts, examples, or source files.
Do not run bulk updates before testing against a small staging dataset.
Do not export sequence, inventory, or ELN data without an approved retention plan.

faq.question: Is this official Benchling software?
faq.answer: No. It is a community skill that explains Benchling integration patterns and references public Benchling documentation.

faq.question: Does this skill access my Benchling tenant automatically?
faq.answer: No. Access requires a tenant URL, credentials, and permissions that the user supplies.

faq.question: What Benchling data types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers registry entities, inventory, ELN entries, workflow tasks, events, and Data Warehouse analytics.

faq.question: How should I handle API keys?
faq.answer: Use a secret manager or environment variables. Never place real keys in prompts, repositories, or shared documents.

faq.question: Can it help with production integrations?
faq.answer: Yes, for planning and implementation guidance. Review scopes, logging, rate limits, retries, and change controls before deployment.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance and examples that developers adapt to their own tenant and schemas.
